issues.description: Import order in test file may not match codebase convention.
issues.detail: The added `import contextlib` is placed between `from argparse import Namespace` and `import io`, mixing `from` and plain imports in the stdlib block. isort/ruff conventions usually group plain imports before from-imports. If the repo's linter is happy, fine; if not, this is the kind of nit CI catches.

The new `.. deprecated:: 4.3` block says 'Use the stlib's' instead of 'stdlib's'. Small thing, but it ships in user-facing docs. Fix it in the same patch — don't make someone send a follow-up patch for one missing 'd'.

issues.description: Deprecation test doesn't assert the warning fires from the documented call site.
issues.detail: `pytest.warns` catches the warning anywhere in the block, including inside `print`. Fine here because only `redirected` warns, but tightening `match=` or using `stacklevel`-aware assertions would make the test less brittle to future refactors. Minor.

review.summary: Small, well-scoped patch. One diff, one purpose: deprecate `falcon.testing.redirected`, point users at stdlib, migrate internal callers, add a deprecation test. This is what a patch should look like — readable, minimal, matches the existing `@deprecated`+news-fragment pattern already used for `httpnow`. Good taste: no new abstraction, just leans on stdlib. Fix the 'stlib' typo and ship it. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK only because of the docstring typo; otherwise ACCEPT.
